jobs.occupation: Associate Digital Product Director – Regulatory Data & AI
jobs.description:
Does it excite you to shape digital products and AI-enabled solutions that make regulatory data flow reliably across the enterprise and on to EMA and FDA, and do you have experience with Veeva Vault RIM? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

Your new position

As Associate Digital Product Director – Regulatory Data & AI, you will drive the evolution of our digital products, enterprise systems and data capabilities, with a primary focus on Regulatory Affairs and Medical Writing and opportunities across the wider organization. A key responsibility is the continued development of regulatory data capabilities in Veeva Vault RIM and other connected Vaults, ensuring that product hierarchies and master data are structured consistently and flow reliably across systems and to health authorities. You will act as business owner of regulatory data, working in close partnership with Digital, Data & Technology (DD&T’s) Data Analytics & AI Platforms team. As our pipeline advances towards late-stage submissions and our digital transformation accelerates, you will build the foundations for connected, data-driven and increasingly AI-enabled business processes that are built on trusted data and responsible AI practices.

We offer exciting responsibilities:

• 
Drive digital product strategy and roadmaps aligned with Zealand’s enterprise data and AI strategy, translating business needs into prioritized initiatives that deliver measurable value

• 
Own the product hierarchy and regulatory master data in Veeva Vault RIM as business data owner, ensuring clear stewardship, accuracy, completeness and consistency across the organization

• 
Connect business-critical regulatory data across Veeva RIM, eTMF and Safety Vaults and, together with DD&T, make it available to enterprise platforms and data lakes, in alignment with regulatory data standards (IDMP, SPOR, xEVMPD, eCTD v4.0), GxP and data integrity requirements for EMA and FDA

• 
Explore and assess generative AI, AI agents, intelligent automation and advanced analytics, and turn promising opportunities into practical solutions for Regulatory Affairs and Medical Writing, through governed AI delivery, together with DD&T and business teams

• 
Define and own regulatory data products, APIs, reporting and business intelligence solutions, built on the shared enterprise data platform with DD&T, that make information more accessible, actionable and reusable across functions

• 
Lead system evolution and cross-functional transformation initiatives, including those supporting Medical Writing, from evaluating new releases and capabilities to implementation, validation, change management and post-launch optimization

Your profile

You are a digitally minded product professional who combines business understanding, systems thinking and technological curiosity. You understand the importance of regulatory data and the processes it supports, and you look beyond individual systems to see opportunities across the wider digital ecosystem. You work independently, bring structure to complex initiatives and build trusted relationships across business and technology teams. You are comfortable owning data in the business and you are curious about how AI, automation and modern data platforms can transform the way we work, and you help colleagues build confidence in new ways of working.

• 
Extensive experience in digital product management, business systems or technology transformation, ideally within pharmaceutical, biotech or another regulated industry

• 
Solid understanding of Regulatory Affairs and the product development lifecycle, including CTAs/INDs, eCTD, submissions and lifecycle management

• 
Experience with complex business applications, data models, master data and cross-system integrations; hands-on experience with Veeva Vault RIM is important, and experience with eTMF or Safety Vaults is an advantage

• 
Ability to define product vision, prioritize competing needs and align business, IT, data and external partners around shared outcomes

• 
Familiarity with APIs, data pipelines, data lakes, business intelligence and tools such as Vault Loader, as well as data governance, data ownership and data product concepts, and an interest in generative AI and intelligent automation

• 
Proven ability to lead complex initiatives independently, including integrations, release management in GxP-validated environments, adoption and change management

Your new team

You will join Regulatory Operations (RegOps), part of Regulatory Affairs & Medical Writing. RegOps is a team of four and the backbone of our regulatory submissions and systems, responsible for Veeva Vault RIM, submission publishing and the regulatory data that supports our pipeline. The team also supports digital and process initiatives within Medical Writing. You will work closely with Regulatory Affairs, Medical Writing, Clinical, Safety, DD&T, the Data Analytics & AI Platforms team and external partners.

Let's bond and be bold

We have a unique culture, characterized by excellent teamwork and strong engagement across the organization. And we want you to help us strengthen this culture.

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let's bond and be bold.

Interested in bonding with us? Then please apply no later than November 11, 2026, or as soon as possible. The applications will be reviewed as they come in. While a cover letter is not required, please include a few sentences in your CV explaining your motivation for applying.

For further information, please contact Head of Regulatory Operations Kristian Kiilerich: kkiilerich@zealandpharma.com.

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

About Zealand Pharma A/S

Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The Company has collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners for research, development, and commercialization. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.

_Would you like to shape the services that help colleagues communicate, collaborate and work productively every day?

_As Service Owner, Collaboration & Productivity, you’ll take end-to-end ownership of these services at GlobalConnect, with Microsoft 365 at the center of your portfolio.

You’ll combine service reliability and governance with the opportunity to shape how our collaboration and productivity services develop over time.

**To Thrive In This Role, You’ll Likely Bring

**

• Several years of experience as a Service Owner, Application Owner, Product Owner or in a similar role, with responsibility for business-critical services or platforms.

• Extensive experience with Microsoft 365 collaboration technologies, including Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online and Microsoft Entra-related dependencies.

• Experience with IT service management and governance, including service transition, incident and problem management, change management and continuous improvement.

• Experience leading cross-functional initiatives and translating business needs into practical, scalable IT solutions.

**About The Role And The Team

**You’ll own the lifecycle of GlobalConnect’s Collaboration & Productivity portfolio, including Microsoft 365, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange Online, Copilot and other strategic collaboration platforms. Your focus will be to keep these business-critical services secure, reliable and well managed, while continuously improving them and helping set the long-term direction for the area.

You’ll be part of the Digital Workplace organization, in a team of 17 colleagues with experience in IT support, system ownership and specialist roles. Working across business and IT, you’ll also partner with Security, Identity Governance & Administration, system owners and external suppliers. Your work will help ensure employees have effective tools for communication, meetings, document collaboration, knowledge sharing and everyday productivity.

**What You’ll Be Working On

**

• Own the service lifecycle across the collaboration and productivity portfolio, ensuring clear governance, documentation, compliance and operational readiness.

• Define and monitor service-level objectives, availability and user experience; follow up on incidents and recurring problems and make improvements.

• Manage licensing, renewals, budget follow-up, cost control and supplier performance.

• Work with business and technical stakeholders to govern access, information sharing, external collaboration, retention and service lifecycles.

• Manage cross-functional change and adoption initiatives, identifying practical opportunities for automation, AI, standardization and better ways of working.

• Act as a subject matter expert and trusted advisor, connecting employee needs with operational, technical, security and strategic priorities.

**Who We Are Looking For

**You bring structure and a pragmatic approach to service management, and you’re comfortable moving between strategic development and day-to-day operational priorities. You build effective working relationships across business and technical teams, and can assess dependencies, risks and competing needs to move work forward. You’re curious about how collaboration services can evolve, including through responsible use of automation and AI.

Does this sound like you? If so, we’d like to hear from you.

**Practical information

**

• The role is based in Denmark.

• GlobalConnect’s standard setup is at least 3 days per week in the office.

• GlobalConnect does not offer relocation packages or work visa sponsorship for this role.

In this role, you’ll have the scope to shape a broad, business-critical portfolio and help make everyday collaboration more secure, reliable and effective for employees.

No need for a personal letter – just send us your CV or LinkedIn profile.

Do you enjoy creating structure in complex projects, bringing business and technology teams together, and turning transformation ambitions into measurable results?

At Sofigate, we combine transformation expertise with modern platforms, data and AI. We are now looking for an experienced Digital Project Manager to join our Copenhagen team and lead customer projects across digital transformation and enterprise technology.

Your role

As a Digital Project Manager, you will lead transformation initiatives from planning through implementation and adoption. Your projects may involve enterprise platforms such as ServiceNow, IT implementations, Process Transformation or AI-enabled solutions.

Working closely with business and technology stakeholders, you will create clarity, maintain momentum and ensure tangible business value—whether you lead an entire project or programme, a transformation workstream or the establishment of effective governance and delivery structures.

What you will do

• Lead digital transformation and enterprise technology projects from initiation to implementation

• Translate business objectives into clear plans, governance and measurable outcomes

• Build trusted relationships with customers and stakeholders across business and IT

• Coordinate multidisciplinary teams and create structure and momentum in complex environments

• Manage scope, timelines, risks, dependencies and decision-making

• Facilitate workshops and steering groups while supporting communication, change and adoption

• Use AI-supported tools to improve planning, reporting, analysis and project delivery

• Contribute to customer roadmaps and identify opportunities for continued business value

What you bring

We value mindset, experience and potential over a perfect checklist. You are proactive, pragmatic and comfortable taking ownership when not everything is defined from the outset.

We imagine that you:

• Have 3–5 years of experience leading digital transformation, technology or platform-related projects

• Understand how business processes, technology and organisational change come together in successful transformations

• Are confident working with stakeholders at different organizational levels across business and IT

• Bring a structured and solution-oriented approach to planning, governance, and delivery

• Communicate complex topics clearly and facilitate effective decision-making

• Are comfortable working with agile, waterfall or hybrid delivery methods

• Are curious about AI, automation and how emerging technologies can create measurable business value

• Have an entrepreneurial mindset, work independently and communicate fluently in Danish and English

Experience with ServiceNow or IT operating-model transformation would be a strong advantage.

Consulting and organizational change management experience are also valuable.

Why Sofigate?

At Sofigate, your growth truly matters. You will join around 20 colleagues in our Copenhagen office in Østerbro, where we have an informal and supportive culture with the freedom to shape your own work and contribute to the growth of our Danish business. At the same time, you will be part of a Nordic community built on collaboration, trust and entrepreneurship.

You will work on meaningful transformation projects across industries, with opportunities to explore leading enterprise platforms and AI-enabled solutions. Through hands-on customer work, knowledge sharing and close collaboration with experienced colleagues across the Nordics, you will continue developing as a consultant and project leader.

We value wellbeing, flexibility, diversity and inclusion, and offer flexible and hybrid ways of working alongside a competitive salary and benefits package.

Our values are dare, care and grow: we challenge established ways of working, care about our customers and colleagues, and grow together.

Ready to lead change with us?

Tell us your story and why you would like to join Sofigate. Please submit your application and CV in English. We review applications continuously and encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

To be considered for the position, you must be legally permitted to live and work in Denmark.

If you have any questions, please contact Nevine Chorbaji, Talent Acquisition Partner, at nevine.chorbaji@sofigate.com.

**About Sofigate

**We are The Business Technology Company with the fastest time-to-value in the generative AI era. By combining transformation expertise with low/no-code platforms and generative AI, we help customers design and implement transformations and business-friendly solutions using platforms such as ServiceNow, Salesforce and SAP.

We founded the Business Technology Forum and developed the Business Technology Standard. Our community of more than 800 professionals works across Finland, Sweden, Denmark, Hungary and Poland, always ready to support our colleagues and customers.

We are more than 800 top notch professionals with diverse backgrounds, working with customers from all sectors and various industries. We are a people business, and we believe it’s our people’s competence that counts.

We want you to add your skills into the mix. At Sofigate, you will find plenty of collective know-how to draw on, along with opportunities to learn and grow

Our values Dare, Care and Grow are visible in our every day life - find out more about Sofigate and join us!

**The Impact You'll Make

**Do you enjoy turning complex technical data into insights that drive better products and smarter decisions? Are you passionate about combining data science with engineering and domain expertise to solve real-world challenges? Then this could be the opportunity for you.

As our Lead Engineer, Data Science, you’ll play a key role in transforming product, sensor and operational data into meaningful insights that support innovation, energy efficiency and data-driven decision-making across Danfoss Climate Solutions.

Working closely with business teams, engineers and data platform specialists, you’ll combine strong analytical capabilities with engineering and domain knowledge to identify high-value opportunities, shape AI and analytics use cases and help build a robust, AI-ready data foundation for future intelligent solutions.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**

• Translate complex business and engineering challenges into analytical questions, data-driven models and actionable insights

• Analyze product, sensor, device and operational data to identify patterns, trends and opportunities for performance and energy optimization

• Apply engineering and domain knowledge to shape high-value data science and AI use cases, including feature definition, hypothesis development and validation strategies

• Collaborate with data engineers and platform teams to improve data quality, accessibility and usability across analytics and data products

• Contribute to semantic models and knowledge graph capabilities that capture relationships between sensors, devices, assets and their operational context

• Communicate insights and recommendations clearly to technical and business stakeholders, helping turn analytical findings into practical business actions

**What We're Looking For

**

• Strong foundation in thermodynamics and physics, with the ability to apply first-principles reasoning to heating and cooling systems and processes

• Experience in data science, applied analytics or similar roles within a technical, industrial or engineering environment

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with proficiency in Python and SQL and the ability to translate engineering insight into data-driven models

• Good understanding of modern data and ML environments, including cloud platforms and the machine learning lifecycle

• Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across engineering, data and business teams

• Experience with HVAC, refrigeration, heating/cooling, energy systems or industrial operational data is considered a strong advantage

**What You'll Get From Us

**

• We promote from within and support your learning with mentoring, training, and access to global opportunities.

• You’ll have flexibility, autonomy, and support to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance. Your well-being matters to us.

• We strive to create an inclusive work environment where people of all backgrounds are respected, and valued for who they are.

• You’ll receive benefits like 13th salary, annual bonus, paid vacation, pension plans, personal insurance, and more. These vary by country and contract, but they’re worth asking about—we think they’re pretty great.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our **FAQ Page.

**All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Some jobs teach you a skill. This one teaches you how to grow. We are looking for a curious, driven Business Development Representative to own outbound in Sweden, part time, from our Copenhagen office.

Who we are

Cludo is a Danish tech company that builds AI powered, intelligent search for content rich websites. The way we all search has changed: we no longer want a list of links, we expect a direct answer. Cludo gives website visitors exactly that, a modern search experience that understands what they are looking for and answers them directly.For communication, marketing and web teams, Cludo is also a platform for insight. They see what their users search for, spot the gaps and use those insights to keep improving both their content and the search experience. Organizations across Europe and beyond trust us to do this, guided by our four values: Growth, Passion, Reason and Sincerity.

Why business development matters here

Business development is the engine of Cludo. Most of our new growth starts with a conversation a BDR opened, which makes this team central to the success of the whole company. It is also one of the few places where you see your impact straight away. In sales you never have to wonder whether you are doing well: the numbers tell you, every single week.

The role: own outbound in Sweden

We opened the Swedish market three years ago, and the foundations are in place: real customers, real references and a proven playbook. Now we are looking for someone to pick up that momentum and own outbound in Sweden. You will work in tandem with our Swedish Account Executive. You open the doors and build the pipeline; they take the opportunities forward to close. Together, you are responsible for growing the Swedish market. Our focus segments are the public sector, higher education, regions, banks and insurance companies.

This is a part time role of around 15 to 20 hours per week, built to fit around your studies. Your hours are flexible, but we want you in our Copenhagen office for most of them, because that is where the learning, the energy and the team are. You report to Matteo Pasquato, who leads our Global BDR team.

What you'll be doing

• 
Own the outbound motion in Sweden, from building target lists to booking the first meeting

• 
Research organizations across the public sector, higher education, regions, banking and insurance, and find the right people to talk to

• 
Start real conversations by phone, email and LinkedIn, and turn curiosity into meetings

• 
Use AI to work smarter and faster: research accounts, find the right organizations and people, and personalize your outreach so every message lands

• 
Qualify opportunities and hand them to your Account Executive with the context they need to win

• 
Plan campaigns together with your AE and adjust them based on what the numbers tell you

• 
Support marketing initiatives in Sweden, both digital and in person

Who you are

Your background matters less than your mindset. We care more about who you are becoming than about what is already on your CV.

• 
Curious. You ask questions, dig deeper and want to understand how things work. The more curious you are, the faster you learn.

• 
Eager to learn. You want to become a better version of yourself every day, and you see feedback as fuel.

• 
Driven. You set goals, chase them and take ownership of your results.

• 
Resilient and consistent. A no does not slow you down for long. You show up with the same energy on the hard days as on the good ones.

• 
Fluent in Swedish and strong in English, both written and spoken.

• 
Organized and analytical, with a love for figuring things out.

A big plus

An additional language beyond Swedish and English. We are continuously experimenting in new markets, so every extra language opens doors, for you and for us. Bonus points too if you have done outreach or customer facing work before, or already know your way around the Swedish public sector.

The team you join

You join Cludo's BDR team: multicultural, made up of people from different countries and backgrounds, and set to grow in number over the coming years. We are the most active, and probably the loudest, team at Cludo. High energy, high tempo.

Three words sum up what we stand for: fresh, energetic and inspirational. Expect shared wins, honest feedback and teammates who pick you up when you need it.

The honest part

This role is not easy. Outbound sales is a game of consistency, and there will be ups and downs: weeks where everything clicks and weeks where nothing seems to land.

What matters is what you do with the downs. Every no teaches you something, and you will never have to figure it out alone. Your manager and your team are there to coach you, back you and help you turn setbacks into progress.

What you take with you

The BDR role is a talent factory and a starting point, not a destination. It is a great first step for any career, whatever your background. The skills you build here, from communication and resilience to structure and discipline, will serve you in your professional life and your private life alike. Whether your next step is in sales or somewhere else entirely, you will carry what you learn here with you.

What we offer

• 
Real impact from day one in a fun, informal and creative environment

• 
Flexible hours that fit around your studies and schedule

• 
A commitment to work life balance, proudly Danish style

• 
A front row seat to see how a tech company scales

• 
A bright, buzzing office in Copenhagen, with daily lunch from our amazing kitchen crew

• 
Onsite perks like a motion room, sauna, winter bathing access and kayaks (yes, really)

• 
Cold dips and breakfast with the team every Friday morning

How we hire

• 
Apply.

• 
First interview. Meet Matteo, Ville (our VP of Sales) and a few of your future teammates (about 1.5 hours).

• 
Culture and context. Wrap up with a conversation with Tina, our Scandinavian AE.

Curious? Apply, and let's see where you get.

We make it easier for visitors to find relevant information via a more natural and intuitive guided website search experience. Headquartered in Copenhagen, we are an ambitious and customer-focused international team. Join us today and help us scale to the next level of success! Every employee at Cludo has the ability to bring meaningful work to their job. A few years into RevOps, most people end up choosing between staying close to admin and reporting, or moving towards building automations and the AI tools that now sit on top of the CRM. The second path is hard to get onto if you haven't done it somewhere first.

In this job you'd do both, in a commercial team that already works with AI day to day through assistants connected to Salesforce, support tickets and product data, while marketing is being rebuilt the same way. You'd build on that, starting next to the person who set most of it up and taking over the technical side from them. You'd also keep the CRM and the data underneath it in good order. That's a lot of upkeep, like permissions, data cleanup and renewal notices to thousands of customers, and there's no ops team to share it with.

Airtame makes wireless screen-sharing devices and the cloud software that manages them, used in schools and workplaces around the world. Most of our volume goes through distributors on several continents, sometimes to customers our own reps sent them. Our sales team also works deals directly, and smaller orders come through our Shopify store. Running all three through one Salesforce makes for a harder data model than most RevOps roles come with.

We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and we'd prefer you to work from the office there. Remote from elsewhere in the EU works too. You'd report to our Director of Customer Experience & Revenue Operations, who sets the roadmap with you and owns the metric definitions, and you'd work with sales, customer experience, marketing and product every week.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

Own the Commercial Stack: By the end of the year the technical side has moved over to you, including the AI tools the team uses. You bring the roadmap to your manager and build it, and when sales or support want a system changed, you decide how it's done.

Send the Right Renewal Message: Thousands of customers receive renewal notices. We're starting to ask customers in our cloud software how they intend to renew, and you'd build the email flows that act on it, with a separate path for each way of renewing. If a notice doesn't go out, you know within hours.

Make the Numbers Agree: Pipeline, bookings, ARR, renewals and churn come out the same in every dashboard and every AI assistant, whether the sale came through Shopify, a rep or a distributor. Your manager sets the definitions, and you make sure every system uses them.

Automate the Manual Work: Find the processes worth automating and keep shipping them, tested in a sandbox first with a way back if something goes wrong. The first one is turning the pricing claims our distributors send, in all sorts of formats, into line-item pricing in Salesforce with an audit trail. As AI assistants get better at connecting to things on their own, part of this is also deciding what's still worth building ourselves.

Bring Support onto Intercom: We're moving customer support from Zendesk to Intercom. Depending on when you join, you'd help finish the move or pick it up just after go-live, then own Intercom, including its Salesforce sync and the AI setup that gets customer feedback to the product team.

Who You Are

• You know Salesforce from the inside. A few years of hands-on admin, including Flow Builder, permissions and the data model. You write SQL and SOQL and can model data for a report yourself.

• You ask why before you build. You can tell us about a request you pushed back on, or a process you changed or dropped instead of automating it as asked, and what it was for in the first place.

• You work with AI by default. You use AI tools every day to write flows and queries, and you keep up with what's new on your own. When a new connector makes something we built unnecessary, you're happy to retire it. If you've connected tools through their APIs or written some Python or JavaScript, that's a strong plus.

• You've run a commercial system on your own. At some point you've been the only or main admin of a Salesforce org or a similar system, and you left documentation behind that someone else could take over from. Here there's no ops team behind you, so a broken sync in the morning and a dashboard request in the afternoon are both yours.

Why Airtame?

• Building on Top of Admin: You'd keep the CRM running and build automations and AI tooling on top of it, starting next to the person who set most of it up.

• Most RevOps roles are purely SaaS or purely e-commerce. Here, you get to solve the unique intellectual challenge of bridging a hardware supply chain with a high-velocity digital subscription model.

• A healthy work-life balance.

• Five weeks paid vacation and 5 days of extra paid AirtameFlex days.

• Pension and private health insurance (on FTE Copenhagen contract).

• Flexible work environment, with a hybrid mindset.

• Catered lunch in the office.

Airtame is an equal opportunity employer. We have colleagues across the globe, with both in-office and full-time remote workers. This feeds into our international hybrid mindset, with people from 25+ nationalities that make up the Airtame team.

Our work-life cultural balance is key to our success. Our team encompasses our values of trust and open communication to support each other and to collaborate in a fun and collective way.

At T-Systems, we help organisations navigate their digital transformation journeys through secure, innovative and future-ready cloud solutions. Our Portfolio Area Cloud plays a key role in driving this transformation, delivering solutions that create real business value for our customers.

In this role you will play a key role in bridging customer needs, cloud technology and business value.

Working closely with our sales teams, architects, delivery specialists and portfolio experts, you will take ownership of designing end-to-end cloud solutions that are technically robust, commercially competitive and ready for successful delivery.

You will be a trusted technical partner throughout the customer engagement, helping translate complex requirements into practical, future-proof solutions.

What you'll be doing

• Design impactful cloud solutions: Develop end-to-end architectures across private, public, hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including cloud migration, modernisation, security and integration.

• Turn customer needs into solutions: Understand business and technical requirements and translate them into scalable, secure and commercially viable cloud designs.

• Shape winning proposals: Partner with sales and bid teams to develop compelling technical solutions, contribute to customer presentations and support complex IT outsourcing opportunities.

• Balance innovation and commercial value: Evaluate solution options, costs, risks and delivery requirements to achieve the right balance between performance, feasibility and business value.

• Collaborate across borders: Work with international teams, delivery units, security specialists and portfolio experts to ensure seamless solution development and handover.

• Stay ahead of the market: Bring industry knowledge, cloud expertise and an understanding of emerging technologies to help strengthen our solutions and competitive positioning.

• Drive continuous improvement: Contribute to architecture standards, solution frameworks and best practices across our Cloud Portfolio.

We are looking for someone who combines strong technical expertise with commercial awareness, a collaborative mindset and a genuine passion for solving customer challenges.

Ideally, you will bring:

• Proven experience in cloud solution design, solution architecture or technical presales, preferably within IT services, managed services or IT outsourcing.

• Great knowledge of private, public and hybrid cloud environments, cloud infrastructure and enterprise IT architectures.

• Experience designing complex end-to-end IT solutions and contributing to technical proposals or large-scale customer engagements.

• The ability to balance technical requirements, commercial considerations, delivery capabilities and customer expectations.

• Great analytical and problem-solving skills, with the confidence to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and business stakeholders.

• Experience collaborating with cross-functional and international teams.

• A proactive, structured and customer-focused approach, with the ability to take ownership and work independently.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

You should also be comfortable working in an international environment and travelling occasionally when required.

Why join T-Systems?

At T-Systems, you will have the opportunity to work on complex and meaningful cloud transformation projects, collaborate with experienced specialists across our international organisation and help shape solutions for leading customers.

You will be part of a business where technical expertise, collaboration and fresh thinking are valued, and where your ideas can contribute to how we develop our cloud services.

We believe that our culture is shaped by the everyday actions of our people. Each of us has the opportunity to make a positive impact on our colleagues, our customers and our business.

Because at T-Systems, our people make the difference. #peoplemakethedifference

If you are excited about combining cloud technology, customer engagement and solution innovation, we would love to hear from you.

jobs.occupation: Solution Architect / IT Solution Owner – ERP-to-Bank
jobs.description:
**Job Description

****Join us in building a new strategic integration capability

**Are you motivated by shaping new solutions from the ground up? Do you enjoy turning complex business ambitions into secure, scalable technology?

We are establishing a new team in the Customer & Sector Integration tribe to accelerate ERP-to-Bank. Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

The Opportunity

Veo runs on a fast-growing estate of devices, SaaS tools and offices across Copenhagen, Berlin and Miami. As the first operational IT security hire, you'll own the security of that environment: the devices our people use, the identities and access that connect them to our tools, and how we respond when something goes wrong.

This isn't a "follow the runbook" role. You'll sit in our IT team, assess where we are today, set the direction, and build the processes and tooling that keep Veo secure as we scale.

What You Will Do

• 
You'll be hands-on across endpoint, identity, and operational security, and you'll be the go-to person for IT security across the business.

• 
Own endpoint security across our macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android devices, including EDR, MDM, patching, encryption and hardening baselines

• 
Define and enforce our BYOD approach, using conditional access, device compliance checks and data separation so people can work flexibly without putting company data at risk

• 
Run SSO, SCIM and MFA across our SaaS applications, and own onboarding and offboarding so access is granted and removed on time, every time.

• 
Build identity governance, including regular access reviews, least-privilege access, and clear ownership of who has access to what

• 
Lead IT incident response from detection and triage through containment, investigation and post-incident review, and keep our playbooks sharp

• 
Monitor and respond to CVEs affecting our endpoints and SaaS tools, assessing risk, prioritizing fixes, and making sure patches are applied on time

• 
Plan and run phishing simulations and security awareness training that change behavior, and measure the results

• 
Drive day-to-day operational security, including alert monitoring, vulnerability management, SaaS vendor assessments, and keeping policies and runbooks current

• 
Lead our IT security work for GDPR and NIS2, from implementing controls to maintaining documentation and evidence, together with Legal and GRC

• 
Help lay the groundwork for future SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certification

• 
Own our office security systems, such as CCTV and door access, working with our Office Manager

What You Could Bring

• 
You've likely spent several years in IT security or security operations, ideally in a growing tech company, and you're comfortable being the person who owns security end-to-end.

That experience tends to show up in several of the following:

• 
Endpoint and device security: hands-on with EDR and MDM tools such as CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Hexnode, Intune or Kandji, across desktop and mobile, including securing BYOD environments

• 
Identity and access: deep experience with Google Workspace and Entra rolling out SSO, SCIM, and MFA, and running joiner/mover/leaver processes and access reviews.

• 
Incident response: you've led real incidents end-to-end and can stay calm and clear under pressure.

• 
Vulnerability management: you track CVEs, judge real-world risk quickly, and get fixes rolled out.

• 
Security culture: you've run phishing awareness programs and can explain risk in plain language to people who aren't technical.

• 
Compliance in practice: you've applied GDPR and NIS2 requirements in an operational role. Experience with SOC 2 or ISO 27001 is a strong advantage as we work towards them.

Linux: administration and hardening experience is highly valued.

Nice To Have

Scripting and automation (Python, PowerShell, Bash)

SIEM experience

Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, OSCP, or GIAC

You'll be part of the IT team within Administration & Finance and work most closely with GRC, the Security Enablement Team, and Legal. We're pragmatic; we prioritize what matters most, and we favor simple solutions that help people work securely without slowing them down.

Pandektes is building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world. Behind it is a backend that has to ingest, structure and search a huge database of legal information.

We’re looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to help us making sure that the legislation and volume of data stays stable so we can scale our services so we can ingest larger volumes of data, more efficiently.

We have recently closed our Series A round and joining now means you will have a big impact how we grow in the future. This role is based in our Copenhagen HQ.

About Pandektes

Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 45+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

The experience you’ll bring

You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Experience integrating AI technologies like OpenAI and Pinecone into production systems to build innovative, data-driven solutions. Experience with vector databases, transformers, NLP and LLMs is a plus.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

What we offer

You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

• Have at least six months of practical experience using agentic AI as part of your software development workflow

• Hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, IT, or a related technical field

• Have strong software engineering fundamentals

• Are comfortable owning complex technical problems and decisions

• Can navigate and improve an established codebase and architecture

• Care about maintainability, reliability, performance, and quality

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve engineering practices beyond your immediate product work

At a big company, the platform layer is a hundred engineers, and you own a slice of it. A driver. A subsystem. A corner of the release pipeline. You go deep, but you rarely get to hold the whole thing. With us you will. One team owns the entire layer: the operating system and firmware on every Airtame, the streaming stack underneath it, the releases that reach devices in the field, and the work of turning new hardware into a shipping product.

The role is roughly 60% hands-on the hardest problems and 40% growing the engineers who work on them.

**About Airtame

**We're around 55 people, headquartered in Copenhagen, and you'd work from there or remotely from within the EU. We make the hardware and the software that runs on it, so a change you make to the firmware ships to every Airtame in the field. The team is cross-functional and spread across Europe, and it reaches a global market from a small base.

Year one outcomes

Take AirPlay and Miracast from beta to default. They're in beta today. A year from now they should be solid enough to ship on by default across the Airtame product line, so customers get them without opting in and never have to think about which protocol they're using. Judge it by connection success rates on the fleet, and by how many customers rely on them day to day.

Make firmware releases boring. The best release is the one nobody has to think about: a predictable cadence, an automated quality bar, and shipping to the whole fleet as routine. A year from now, cutting a release should be a low-drama process the team trusts, and that should let you ship improvements more often. Judge it by release frequency, and by the confidence behind each one.

Turn the next board into a shipping Airtame. New silicon has to boot, hold a network, manage its heat, and run conferencing well enough to sell. By year-end there's a repeatable path from a board landing on a desk to a build QA can test, and you own it. Judge it by how long that path takes, and whether the thermal and acoustic targets hold.

Lead the team. You'll run the 1:1s, set the technical bar, and support team members' growth. The measure is simple: a year in, the team runs on your leadership day to day.

Push AI-assisted development further. The team already builds with AI daily. You'll lead the next step: sharper workflows, better tooling choices, new patterns that make the whole group faster. By year-end, the team's AI practices should be visibly ahead of where they started.

Who you are

• The player-coach. You've set a team's technical direction: the architecture calls, the reviews where the hard problems get caught. And you want the people side too. Growing engineers, running 1:1s, hiring. You're not looking to trade one for the other. Maybe you've been a staff engineer or tech lead ready to own a team, or a manager who never stopped writing code. Either way, 60/40 sounds about right to you.

• At home where software meets hardware. Embedded Linux is your familiar ground: the kernel, the BSP, userspace, C and C++ running on the device itself. You've spent time close to the metal: wireless stacks, streaming protocols, drivers. You can reason about a bug whether it lives in the firmware, the network, or the silicon.

• You ship to hardware you can't reach. When it's firmware on a device mounted in someone's meeting room, a bad release doesn't just roll back with a hotfix. You've owned software that ships to the field, so staged rollouts, over-the-air updates, and testing on the devices themselves come naturally. "Works on my bench" isn't the finish line for you.

• You've turned new hardware into a product. Bare silicon arrives, and someone has to make it boot, talk to the network, manage its heat, and eventually stream. You've done that kind of bringup, or worked close enough to it to lead the people who do.

• You use AI as a daily tool. You write code with it, debug with it, prototype with it. You've formed your own view on where it speeds things up and where it gets in the way, and you help the people around you do the same.
